findings.title: Security group ingress open to the world
findings.description: Ingress rules allowing 0.0.0.0/0 expose the workload to the entire internet. Restrict source CIDRs to known ranges.
findings.remediation:
Restrict the ingress CIDR to trusted ranges. Replace `0.0.0.0/0` with your
office/VPN CIDRs, or remove the rule and use SSM Session Manager (no inbound
SSH needed):
ingress {
  from_port   = 22
  to_port     = 22
  protocol    = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks = ["203.0.113.0/24"]  # your trusted range
}

findings.title: IAM role uses an inline policy
findings.description: The role embeds an inline policy document instead of attaching a managed policy. Inline policies cannot be reused, versioned, or reviewed centrally. Prefer aws_iam_policy with aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: IAM role has no permissions boundary
findings.description: The role sets no permissions_boundary, so nothing caps the maximum permissions its policies can grant — a single overly broad policy attachment becomes fully effective. Set a permissions boundary as a guardrail.

findings.title: IAM role has no description
findings.description: The IAM role has no description, so reviewers cannot tell what the role is for or who owns it. Document the role's purpose in the description field.

findings.title: Redis cache with non-SSL port enabled
findings.description: azurerm_redis_cache with enable_non_ssl_port = true accepts plaintext Redis connections, exposing credentials and data in transit.
findings.remediation: Enforce TLS 1.2+. Set `min_tls_version = "TLS1_2"` / `minimum_tls_version = "1.2"`, replace HTTP listeners with HTTPS, and redirect HTTP→HTTPS. Disable weak ciphers and old protocol versions.
